_about: Weights and rules for tools/retention_score.py. Every rule names the ranking signal it serves and whether it rests on evidence or inference. tools/feedback_loop.py (Component 4) recalibrates the weights against real channel data; until then these are priors, not measurements.

swipe_away.name: Viewed vs. swiped away
swipe_away.what: Share of feed impressions where the viewer chose to watch instead of swiping past. Decided in the first ~2 seconds.
swipe_away.source: YouTube Studio metric for Shorts ('How many chose to view'), announced by YouTube: https://support.google.com/youtube/community-video/273390203/new-youtube-shorts-metric-viewed-vs-swiped-away

avg_pct_viewed.name: Average percentage viewed
avg_pct_viewed.what: How much of the Short the average viewer watches. A loop that triggers a rewatch can push it above 100%.
avg_pct_viewed.basis: evidence for the metric, inference for its ranking weight
avg_pct_viewed.source: averageViewPercentage is a YouTube Analytics API core metric: https://developers.google.com/youtube/analytics/channel_reports . YouTube does not publish how heavily Shorts ranking weights it; 'retention over views' is the consensus of creator-side analysis, not an official statement.

replays.name: Replays
replays.what: Since 31 March 2025 a Shorts view counts every start or replay, so a seamless loop produces counted rewatches.
replays.basis: evidence for the counting change, inference for the ranking effect

_pace_source: Measured: Cosmic Short #1 voiceover, 63 spoken words in 25.5s (docs/IMAGE_PROMPTS_FLUX_COSMIC.md). Recalibrate if the voice changes.

section_weights._signal: Hook carries swipe_away; body and ending carry avg_pct_viewed and replays. Hook weighted hardest because a viewer lost there never reaches any other beat. Inference.

promise_in_window.why: Something must be promised before the swipe decision, roughly 2s in.

subject_in_hook.why: The viewer has to know what the video is about inside the hook sentence.

no_setup_opener.why: Openers like 'Scientists have long…' or 'Did you know' spend the 2s window on context instead of outcome.

hook_brevity.why: A hook sentence over ~14 words (~6s) delays the first payoff.

opens_loop.why: Raises a question, stake or unexplained term the viewer wants resolved.

closes_loop.why: Pays off something already promised with a concrete fact, so the promise felt worth keeping.

carry.why: Gives a concrete reason to stay into the next beat: an escalation, a 'then', an unanswered consequence.

loops_to_hook.why: Last line echoes the hook so the cut back to frame 1 reads as continuous.

lands_new_turn.why: Ends on a final twist or implication, not a restated fact.

no_outro.why: 'Subscribe' or 'thanks for watching' breaks the loop and signals the video is over.

length.name: Runtime outside 20-35s
length.source: docs/GROWTH_STRATEGY.md section 5 (repo guidance, not external research)
